articles.title: How to Get a Number Row on Your iPhone Keyboard
articles.description: Want numbers above the letters on iPhone? Learn what Apple’s standard keyboard offers, a quicker way to type digits, and when a number-row keyboard helps.
articles.deck: Options for typing numbers without constantly switching between letters and digits.
articles.answer: On the standard English iPhone keyboard, there is no setting that adds a permanent number row above the letters. You can switch with the 123 key, use a press-and-slide gesture for a single digit, or choose a third-party keyboard with a number row. Layouts vary by language, app, and device; the iPad keyboard is different.
sections: apple-keyboard
Can you add a number row to Apple’s iPhone keyboard?

For the standard English letter layout, Apple does not offer a “show number row” toggle. The number and symbol layout is a separate view, opened with 123. Changing keyboard feedback, predictive text, or one-handed mode does not add another row of keys.

Some apps request a numeric keypad for a phone number, amount, or code. That keypad belongs to that input field; it does not change your letter keyboard everywhere else. Instructions for an iPad’s number gestures also do not necessarily apply to an iPhone.
single-number
A faster way to type one number

If you only need an occasional digit, try this with Apple’s standard English keyboard:

  1. In a normal text field, touch and hold 123.
  2. Without lifting your finger, slide to the number you want.
  3. Lift your finger to enter it and return to the letter layout.

For several digits in a row, simply tap 123, type the numbers, and tap ABC to return. The press-and-slide gesture is a useful shortcut, but it is not a persistent number row. Keyboard layouts and gesture behavior can differ, so try it in a note before relying on it in another app.
number-row-keyboard
When a dedicated number row helps

If you frequently mix letters and numbers—street addresses, product names, reference numbers, or dates—a visible row can reduce layout switching. The tradeoff is space: an extra row can take more screen height or require a denser layout.

Typez includes a number row above the letters, alongside precise cursor controls and saved text. This guide is published by Typez’s creator, so that recommendation is our own product. Typez is currently in App Store review; join the waitlist for a TestFlight invitation if you want to try it.

Use a keyboard that fits the text you write most often. A person who mainly writes messages may prefer a simpler layout; someone repeatedly entering mixed codes may value the extra row more.
enable-keyboard
How to enable another keyboard

After installing a keyboard app, open Settings → General → Keyboard → Keyboards → Add New Keyboard and select it. Open a text field, touch and hold the globe key, and choose the keyboard. See Typez setup help for the Typez-specific steps.

A third-party keyboard will not appear in every field. iOS uses its own keyboard for secure input and certain phone pads, and an app can disallow custom keyboards. That means a number-row keyboard cannot promise the same layout everywhere.
permissions
Do you need Full Access just for a number row?

An extra row of keys does not inherently require network access. Permissions depend on the keyboard and the feature. In Typez, core typing and cursor navigation work without Full Access; optional clipboard functionality requires it because of iOS restrictions.

Review the app’s privacy policy rather than enabling permissions just because a tutorial says to. Typez’s privacy policy explains the difference between typing and clipboard access.
other-options
An alternative for numbers you repeat

A number row helps you enter new text. It may not be the quickest answer for an address or reference string you reuse unchanged. Apple’s Text Replacement can expand a shortcut into a phrase; saved text can insert an item you deliberately kept.

Our iPhone clipboard-history guide compares Notes, Text Replacement, and Typez’s saved-text clipboard. None restores an older clipboard item that was overwritten before you saved it.

articles.title: What Does Allow Full Access Mean for iPhone Keyboards?
articles.description: Understand the iPhone keyboard Full Access warning, which permissions it expands, what it does not prove, and how Typez handles typing and saved text.
articles.deck: What the permission enables, why iOS warns you, and what to check before you turn it on.
articles.answer: Allow Full Access expands what a third-party iPhone keyboard can do, including network access and sharing data with its containing app. It is a permission, not proof that the keyboard sends your typing anywhere. Whether an app collects or transmits data depends on its implementation and policies. You can leave it off when you do not need the features that require it.
sections: meaning
What changes when you allow Full Access?

A third-party keyboard runs as an extension with restrictions. Apple documents that requesting open access expands its sandbox, allowing capabilities such as network access and a shared container with the keyboard’s main app.

Those capabilities can support legitimate features, but they create a reason to choose the developer carefully. A permission being available does not tell you how the developer uses it, and a privacy-friendly slogan does not replace an explanation.

Apple’s documentation for custom keyboards is archived and uses some older interface terminology. It is useful for the permission model; use the current iPhone Settings interface for the steps below.
warning
Does Full Access mean the app reads everything I type?

Do not read Apple’s warning as a report that a particular app has already uploaded your text. It describes a capability and the trust involved in granting it. A keyboard receives input while you use it; network permission can allow that input to be sent off the device if its developer implements that behavior.

Secure text fields use Apple’s system keyboard instead of a custom keyboard. Apps can also block custom keyboards. Those restrictions are useful, but they are not a reason to ignore the privacy practices of a keyboard you use for ordinary messages.
check-policy
What to check before enabling it

• Typed content: Does the developer explicitly say whether it collects or sends the text you enter?
  • Copied text: Are imports deliberate, or does the product claim to capture copies automatically?
  • Storage: Are saved items local, synced, or uploaded? What happens when you delete the app?
  • Other data: Analytics and crash reports are separate from message contents. Check both.
  • Feature need: Which feature stops working with Full Access off?

The App Store privacy label is a useful starting point, alongside the full policy. Neither a permission toggle nor a marketing label is an independent security audit.
typez
How Typez uses Full Access

Typez’s core typing and cursor navigation work without Full Access. Optional clipboard functionality, including making saved items available inside the keyboard, needs Full Access because of iOS restrictions.

Typez reads clipboard text after you choose an import action. Saved clipboard items stay on the device. Enabling Full Access does not cause Typez to upload typing or clipboard contents, and those contents are not included in analytics. Typez does use other app analytics and purchase services, described in the privacy policy.

This guide is published by Typez’s creator. Typez is currently in App Store review; join the waitlist for a TestFlight invitation to try it.
settings
How to turn Full Access on or off

1. Open iPhone Settings.
  2. Go to General → Keyboard → Keyboards.
  3. Select the third-party keyboard.
  4. Change Allow Full Access. Read and consider the system warning before confirming.

If the keyboard is missing, install its app and add it through Add New Keyboard first. The toggle’s availability depends on what the keyboard requests. For Typez, see setup and permission help.

Turning permission off does not retract data a service previously received. If you stop using an app, check its deletion process as well.
clipboard
Full Access does not create clipboard history

Enabling the permission does not give a keyboard a retrospective list of text you copied before installing it. It also does not turn an iPhone into a device with a built-in clipboard-history screen.

Typez deliberately imports items you choose to save. Read what iPhone clipboard history can and cannot do before expecting an app to recover overwritten text.

articles.title: Why Does iPhone Keep Switching Back to Apple’s Keyboard?
articles.description: Find out why your iPhone switches away from a third-party keyboard, when that is expected, and which setup checks can help without deleting saved data.
articles.deck: Some switches are expected iOS behavior. Here is how to tell them apart from a setup problem.
articles.answer: iPhone temporarily uses Apple’s keyboard for secure text fields and certain phone pads, even when you selected a third-party keyboard. An app can also disallow custom keyboards. If the switch happens in ordinary text fields across multiple apps, check that your keyboard is enabled, select it again with the globe key, and check for app or iOS updates. Full Access does not override these restrictions.
sections: expected-switches
When switching to Apple’s keyboard is expected

Apple’s custom-keyboard documentation describes three important limits:

  • Secure text fields: The system replaces a custom keyboard when a field is marked as secure, commonly for a password.
  • Phone-pad fields: Certain input types use the system’s phone keypad.
  • Apps that block extensions: An app developer can reject custom keyboards throughout the app.

Apple’s developer explanation is archived, but it documents the reason these changes can occur. Field configuration matters: do not assume every code box, banking app, or login screen behaves identically.

If your keyboard returns when you move from a protected field to a normal message field, that is consistent with iOS temporarily substituting its own keyboard.
compare-fields
First, compare two ordinary text fields

Before changing settings, identify where the problem happens. Open a normal note and select your keyboard, then try an ordinary message field in another app.

  • If the keyboard works in both but disappears in one particular app, the issue may be the app or its field restrictions.
  • If it disappears only in a password or phone-number field, the switch may be expected.
  • If it repeatedly disappears in normal fields across apps, investigate setup, updates, or a possible extension problem.

This comparison narrows the issue; it does not by itself diagnose a crash. Record the app and field where the switch occurs so support can reproduce it.
select-keyboard
Check that the keyboard is installed and selected

1. Open Settings → General → Keyboard → Keyboards.
  2. Confirm your keyboard is listed. If needed, use Add New Keyboard to add it.
  3. Open a normal text field.
  4. Touch and hold the globe key and choose your keyboard from the list.

You can use the keyboard list’s editing controls to change the order of your enabled keyboards. Treat that as an ordering preference, not a way to bypass secure fields or an app’s restrictions.

For Typez-specific installation steps, visit Typez support.
full-access
Will Full Access stop the switching?

No. Full Access expands a keyboard extension’s permissions; it does not force apps to accept it or let it replace the system keyboard in restricted fields.

Do not enable the permission solely to fix an expected switch in a password field. In Typez, core typing and cursor navigation work without Full Access, while optional clipboard functionality requires it. The privacy policy describes that distinction.
persistent-problem
If it still switches in ordinary text fields

Check for updates to the keyboard app, the affected app, and iOS. Open the keyboard’s containing app once and follow any setup instructions it provides. If the issue persists, restart the iPhone and repeat the two-field comparison.

A keyboard extension that stops unexpectedly is a possible explanation, not a conclusion you can draw from a layout change alone. When contacting support, include your iPhone model, iOS version, keyboard version, affected app, and whether it happens in Notes too. Do not send passwords or private message contents as test material.

Avoid deleting the keyboard app as your first troubleshooting step. In Typez, saved clipboard items are local, and removing the app can remove those items. Keep another copy of anything important.
typez
What to expect when using Typez

Typez is a third-party iPhone keyboard, so it follows these system restrictions too. Its cursor controls, number row, and saved-text clipboard do not override an app’s decision to use Apple’s keyboard.

This guide is published by Typez’s creator. Typez is currently in App Store review; join the waitlist for a TestFlight invitation. For help with saved items, read our iPhone clipboard-history guide before trying an uninstall.

articles.title: How to Move the Cursor Precisely on iPhone
articles.description: Move the iPhone cursor between letters using the spacebar trackpad, direct touch, or a keyboard with arrow keys. Learn which method works best for small edits.
articles.deck: Fix a typo in the middle of a word without deleting everything after it.
articles.answer: Touch and hold the spacebar on Apple’s iPhone keyboard until the keys go blank. Drag to move the cursor, then release. You can also drag the insertion point directly in the text. If you prefer arrow keys, Typez lets you move one character or one word at a time.
sections: spacebar-trackpad
Move the cursor with the spacebar

Trying to tap between two letters often places the cursor at the wrong end of a word. The built-in trackpad is usually a better starting point.

  1. Tap the text you want to edit so the keyboard appears.
  2. Press and hold the spacebar until the key labels disappear.
  3. Without lifting your finger, slide it in the direction you want the cursor to move.
  4. Release when the cursor reaches the correct position.

Try it in Notes with a long sentence. Move slowly when you are close to the letter you want to correct.
direct-placement
Place the cursor between two letters

You can also touch and hold the insertion point in editable text, then drag it to the correct spot. A magnified view can help you see the letters while your finger is over them.

For example, if you typed recieve, position the cursor near the incorrect letters and make the correction. If the entire word is wrong, double-tap it and replace it instead.
character-word-controls
Use arrow keys for precise cursor movement

Apple’s standard iPhone letter keyboard does not have a dedicated row of cursor arrow keys. Typez takes a different approach: you can move left or right by one character, move by whole words, or hold a control to keep moving.

Character controls are useful for punctuation, typos, URLs and codes. Word controls help you move across a longer sentence without dragging the cursor the entire distance.

For another look at Typez, see my original keyboard demo on X (Twitter). These are product demonstrations, not controlled speed tests.
choose-the-edit
Try these three everyday edits

• Missing punctuation: change 630 to 6:30 by inserting the colon in the middle.
  • Wrong character in a link: move to the specific character instead of deleting the rest of the URL.
  • Wrong date: navigate to the date and replace only the part that needs changing.

For isolated edits, the spacebar gesture may be all you need. If you make small corrections repeatedly, dedicated cursor buttons are worth trying.
when-it-does-not-work
Why is the iPhone cursor difficult to move?

If direct tapping keeps selecting a word or moving to its edge, try the spacebar gesture instead. If a third-party keyboard is missing, test it in Notes; password fields and some other fields require Apple’s keyboard.

Typez offers character and word controls without requiring Full Access. Visit the Typez homepage to check availability and join the waitlist for TestFlight.

articles.title: How to Save Frequently Used Text and Phrases on iPhone
articles.description: Save frequently used phrases, addresses, email templates and links on iPhone with Text Replacement, Notes or a clipboard keyboard.
articles.deck: Stop typing the same addresses, links and replies over and over.
articles.answer: Use iPhone Text Replacement for short phrases you can trigger with a shortcut. For longer templates, keep them in Notes. If you want to browse and insert saved text directly from the keyboard, use a saved-text keyboard such as Typez.
sections: choose-reusable-text
What text should you save?

Start with text you type or paste several times a week: your email address, business address, appointment link, a standard reply, or a message template.

Keep the reusable part separate from names, dates and other details that change. Do not store passwords, verification codes or private customer information in general-purpose templates.
text-replacement
Use iPhone Text Replacement for quick shortcuts

1. Open Settings → General → Keyboard → Text Replacement.
  2. Tap +.
  3. Enter the text you want to reuse in Phrase.
  4. Enter an abbreviation in Shortcut and tap Save.
  5. Try the abbreviation with Apple’s keyboard in Notes.

For example, use zzmail for your email address or zzbook for an appointment link. A distinctive prefix helps prevent accidental expansion while typing ordinary words.
practical-templates
Examples of reusable phrases and replies

• Email: your business email address.
  • Booking: “You can choose a time here: [link].”
  • Support: “Could you send your reference number and a short description of the problem?”
  • Availability: “We’re available [days] from [hours].”
  • Address: your office or delivery address.

Replace placeholders and read the message before sending it.
notes-and-typez
Compare Text Replacement, Notes and a clipboard keyboard

MethodBest forTrade-off
Text ReplacementShort phrases and email addressesRemember a shortcut for each phrase
NotesLong templates and organized reference textSwitch apps and copy the text
TypezBrowsing pinned replies, links and addresses inside the keyboardRequires setup; clipboard requires Full Access

If you prefer seeing a list rather than remembering abbreviations, Typez lets you copy a phrase, import it into the clipboard, pin it and insert it from the keyboard the next time you need it.

Items are saved on your device after you deliberately import them. Read the Full Access guide before enabling the clipboard feature.
review-before-sending
Can you save multiple copied texts on iPhone?

Apple’s normal Paste action uses the current clipboard item, not a browsable history of previous copies. If you want to keep multiple texts for later, save each one deliberately using Notes or a clipboard keyboard.

See our guide to iPhone clipboard history for the distinction between copying and saving. Keep a separate backup of important templates, since deleting Typez can remove its locally stored items.

Want your favorite phrases available while typing? See the Typez clipboard and check availability.

articles.title: How to Select, Highlight, and Edit Text on iPhone
articles.description: Learn to select a word or paragraph on iPhone, drag selection handles, highlight a precise range with the keyboard trackpad, and replace or copy text.
articles.deck: Select exactly the text you need and leave the rest untouched.
articles.answer: Double-tap a word in an editable text field to select it. Drag the selection handles to change the highlighted range, then type, cut or paste as needed. To select text with the keyboard, hold the spacebar and use a second finger while moving the first.
sections: cursor-or-selection
Moving the cursor vs selecting text

The cursor marks where new characters will go. Selected text is the range you can copy, cut or replace. For a missing letter, move the cursor; for a wrong word, select it.

See our precise iPhone cursor guide if you only need to move the insertion point.
select-a-word
How to highlight a word or paragraph

1. Open an editable note or message.
  2. Double-tap a word to select it.
  3. Drag the handles at either end to adjust the highlighted range.
  4. Check the selected text before applying an editing command.

In supported fields, triple-tapping selects a paragraph. For a long passage, start with one word and extend the handles. Highlighting here means selecting text for editing, not applying a colored highlight in a document.
trackpad-selection
Select text with the spacebar trackpad

If the handles are difficult to drag precisely, Apple’s keyboard also supports trackpad selection:

  1. Hold the spacebar until the keyboard switches to trackpad mode.
  2. Keep the first finger on the keyboard and touch it with a second finger.
  3. Move the first finger to extend or reduce the selection.
  4. Release when the desired text is selected.

Practice in Notes first. Some custom editors use different selection controls.
replace-selected-text
Replace a word without deleting the whole sentence

Imagine you wrote “Please send the form on Tuesday.” Double-tap Tuesday and type Friday. The rest of the sentence stays intact.

When text is selected, typing or pasting usually replaces it. Check that the selection has not swallowed surrounding spaces or punctuation.
copy-cut-paste
How to copy, cut or paste selected text

• Copy: keeps the original text and places a copy on the clipboard.
  • Cut: removes the selected editable text and places it on the clipboard.
  • Paste: inserts the current copied item, replacing highlighted text if there is a selection.

Look for additional commands in the editing menu if you cannot see the one you want.
keyboard-and-app-limits
What a keyboard can and cannot do

Selection handles and editing menus are provided by the app’s text editor. Typez’s cursor buttons help position the cursor, but they do not replace the host app’s selection tools.

If you frequently correct individual letters or reuse copied phrases, explore the cursor controls and clipboard guide.

articles.title: How to Undo Typing and Accidental Text Deletion on iPhone
articles.description: Undo typing on iPhone with three-finger gestures, Shake to Undo or app controls. Learn what can be restored after accidentally deleting text.
articles.deck: Deleted part of a message? Try undo before you make another edit.
articles.answer: In a supported iPhone text editor, swipe left with three fingers and confirm Undo if prompted. Swipe right to redo. You can also use an app’s undo button or Shake to Undo when enabled. This restores recent edits only when the editor still has the relevant history.
sections: try-undo-first
What to do immediately after deleting text

Keep the affected note, message draft or text field open. Avoid typing more or closing the app until you have tried its undo controls.

If the app has an undo button, start there. If you deleted an entire note or message rather than editing its contents, look for that app’s recovery tools instead.
three-finger-gestures
Undo typing without shaking your iPhone

1. Keep the editable text field active.
  2. Swipe left using three fingers, then tap Undo if the control appears.
  3. Check whether the missing text has returned.
  4. To reverse an undo, try swiping right with three fingers and use Redo if prompted.

A three-finger tap can also bring up editing controls in supported apps. Use the visible undo or redo command if it appears.
shake-to-undo
How to enable Shake to Undo

1. Open Settings → Accessibility → Touch.
  2. Turn on Shake to Undo.
  3. Return to the text you were editing and gently shake the iPhone.
  4. Confirm Undo if the prompt appears.

If you trigger it accidentally, turn it off in the same settings screen and use editing gestures instead.
know-the-limits
Can you recover accidentally deleted text?

Undo may restore a deleted sentence or reverse a paste if the editing session still holds that action. It cannot guarantee recovery after closing a document, restarting an app or deleting the entire item.

  • Deleted notes or files: look for the relevant Recently Deleted or recovery folder.
  • Sent messages: check the messaging app’s edit or unsend options.
  • Overwritten clipboard: undo does not provide a system-wide history of copied items.
protect-reusable-text
Avoid losing important text again

For long drafts, keep a separate copy before making large changes. For phrases you reuse, save them intentionally rather than relying on the clipboard or undo history.

See how to select and edit text safely and our explanation of what iPhone clipboard history can and cannot recover.

Apple: Adjust how iPhone responds to your touch

articles.title: How to Change, Switch, and Reorder Keyboards on iPhone
articles.description: Add a language or third-party keyboard on iPhone, switch using the globe key, change keyboard order and remove unused keyboards.
articles.deck: Choose the keyboard you want without cycling through every layout.
articles.answer: Hold the globe key while typing and select a keyboard from the menu. To add, remove or reorder keyboards, open Settings → General → Keyboard → Keyboards. Installing a third-party keyboard app alone does not enable it.
sections: add-a-keyboard
How to add a new keyboard on iPhone

1. For a third-party keyboard, install its app first.
  2. Go to Settings → General → Keyboard → Keyboards.
  3. Tap Add New Keyboard.
  4. Choose the language layout or installed keyboard you want.

Adding another Apple language keyboard does not add that language to every third-party keyboard. Check the keyboard app’s supported languages separately.
switch-with-globe
How to switch keyboards using the globe key

Open a message or note, then touch and hold the globe or emoji switching control. Select the keyboard by name. A short tap can cycle to the next keyboard; holding the key is useful when several are enabled.

If the keyboard is missing, go back to Settings and make sure it was added.
change-order
How to change the order of iPhone keyboards

1. Open Settings → General → Keyboard → Keyboards.
  2. Tap Edit.
  3. Use the reorder handle to move your preferred keyboards higher in the list.
  4. Tap Done.

This changes the list order, not a system-wide rule that forces one keyboard to stay active in every app.
remove-keyboard
Remove keyboards you do not use

In the same keyboard list, tap Edit and use the remove control beside the unwanted layout. Removing the enabled keyboard is different from uninstalling its app.

Before uninstalling a third-party keyboard, back up anything important that the app stores locally, such as saved text.
why-it-switches
Why does iPhone keep going back to Apple’s keyboard?

iOS can require its own keyboard in protected fields, certain phone-number fields, and apps that disable custom keyboards. Keyboard order and Full Access do not override those restrictions.

If your keyboard disappears in an ordinary text field, follow our keyboard switching troubleshooting guide.
using-typez
How to switch to Typez

Once Typez is installed and enabled, select it from the globe menu just like another keyboard. It offers cursor controls, a number row and a saved-text clipboard.

See setup instructions and the Full Access guide if you plan to enable clipboard functionality.
sources: Apple: Add or change keyboards on iPhone

articles.title: How to Type Numbers and Symbols on iPhone Without Switching Keyboards
articles.description: Use the iPhone 123-key slide gesture, hidden symbols, long-press shortcuts and punctuation tricks to enter characters without repeatedly changing layouts.
articles.deck: Enter an occasional number or symbol and return straight to typing letters.
articles.answer: On Apple’s standard iPhone keyboard, touch and hold the 123 key, slide to a number or punctuation mark, and release. The letter layout returns automatically. For hidden symbols, hold the related key and slide to the character you need.
sections: find-the-layout
Type a number with the 123-key slide gesture

1. Start on the standard English letter keyboard.
  2. Touch and hold 123 without lifting your finger.
  3. Slide to the digit or common punctuation mark you need.
  4. Release to insert it and return to the letter layout.

For example, try typing “Room 7B” using the gesture for the 7. For several consecutive digits, opening the number layout normally may be easier.
hold-for-alternatives
Find hidden symbols and special characters

Hold a related key to see its available variants. Then slide to the character you want before releasing.

  • Hold 0 for the degree symbol (°).
  • Hold a currency symbol to find additional currencies.
  • Hold a letter such as e for accented versions.
  • Open #+= for additional symbols not visible on the first number layout.

The exact long-press choices depend on the keyboard language.
capitals-and-periods
Use shortcuts for capitals and punctuation

For a single uppercase letter, hold Shift, slide to the letter and release. Double-tap Shift for Caps Lock if you need a longer uppercase sequence.

To insert a period followed by a space, double-tap the spacebar with the period shortcut enabled. You can check that option under Settings → General → Keyboard.
repeat-strings
Use shortcuts for strings you type repeatedly

For a frequently entered address, URL or reference phrase, saving the entire string can be faster than entering each character individually. Apple’s Text Replacement and saved-text keyboards provide different ways to do this.

See how to save frequently used text on iPhone for practical examples.
typez-fit
When a permanent number row makes more sense

The 123-key trick helps with occasional digits, but it still requires a gesture. If you frequently type mixed text such as dates, addresses or product codes, Typez keeps a number row above the letters.

Read our separate guide to getting a permanent iPhone keyboard number row for keyboard options. That is a different solution from learning the built-in gestures.

articles.title: How to Turn On or Off iPhone Keyboard Sound and Vibration
articles.description: Change iPhone keyboard clicks and haptic feedback, turn either off, and fix keyboard sound or vibration that is not working.
articles.deck: Make typing quieter or enable a subtle vibration with each keypress.
articles.answer: Open Settings → Sounds & Haptics → Keyboard Feedback. Turn Sound on or off for keyboard clicks, and Haptic on or off for keypress vibration. These are separate switches for Apple’s keyboard.
sections: change-settings
How to change iPhone keyboard sound and vibration

1. Open Settings.
  2. Tap Sounds & Haptics.
  3. Choose Keyboard Feedback.
  4. Toggle Sound for clicks or Haptic for vibration.
  5. Open Notes to test the result.

For silent typing with a physical response, turn Sound off and Haptic on. For no keyboard feedback at all, turn both off.
no-keyboard-sound
iPhone keyboard sound not working?

Check that Sound is enabled under Keyboard Feedback. Then check Silent mode and your sound settings. Test Apple’s keyboard in an ordinary note to separate system settings from an app-specific problem.

If you are using a third-party keyboard, look for its own sound setting.
no-keyboard-haptics
iPhone keyboard vibration not working?

1. Make sure Haptic is enabled under Keyboard Feedback.
  2. Open Settings → Accessibility → Touch.
  3. Check whether Vibration is turned on.
  4. Test typing again in Notes.

The accessibility vibration switch affects more than keyboard feedback, so consider that before changing it.
sound-vs-haptics
Does keyboard vibration affect battery life?
Apple notes that keyboard haptics may affect battery life. It does not specify a fixed percentage. If you do not find the feedback useful, turning it off is a reasonable choice.
third-party-keyboards
Why feedback can differ on a third-party keyboard

Custom keyboards can provide their own sound and vibration preferences. Typez includes keyboard feedback customization alongside theme and font options. Check the settings in your installed version rather than assuming the Apple keyboard toggles apply to it.
sources: Apple: Change iPhone keyboard sounds or haptics

articles.title: Apple Keyboard vs Third-Party Keyboards: What’s the Difference?
articles.description: Compare Apple’s built-in iPhone keyboard with third-party keyboards for cursor control, clipboard features, number rows, autocorrection, privacy and compatibility.
articles.deck: Find out when the built-in keyboard is enough and when an alternative makes sense.
articles.answer: Apple’s keyboard is built into iOS and offers familiar typing tools, autocorrection and a spacebar trackpad. Third-party keyboards can add features such as cursor arrows, saved text, different layouts or more customization. They also have separate permissions and cannot replace Apple’s keyboard in every field.
sections: comparison-method
What changes when you install a third-party keyboard?

A third-party keyboard is an alternative typing interface that you install and enable on your iPhone. It can change the layout and offer additional tools within the keyboard area, but it does not take control of every text field or system feature.

This guide is written by the developer of Typez. It explains feature differences rather than ranking keyboards by measured typing speed or accuracy.
feature-comparison
Apple keyboard vs third-party keyboard features

FeatureApple keyboardThird-party keyboards
Cursor movementSpacebar trackpad and text editing controlsMay offer dedicated cursor buttons or other gestures
Saved textText Replacement and current clipboardSome offer browsable saved text or clipboard tools
Number entrySeparate number layout on standard English keyboardSome offer a permanent number row
Autocorrection and predictionsBuilt-in, depending on language and settingsVaries by app and language
Swipe typingQuickPath on supported languagesAvailable in some apps
CustomizationSystem keyboard settings and supported layoutsMay offer themes, fonts and feedback settings
PrivacyBuilt into iOSReview app privacy policy and optional Full Access
CompatibilitySystem keyboardCan be unavailable in protected fields

These are categories of possible features, not capabilities guaranteed by every third-party keyboard.
cursor-movement
Cursor control and saved text: where alternatives help

Apple’s spacebar trackpad works well for occasional corrections. If you regularly edit a URL, code or small typo, Typez offers explicit character and word controls instead. See the original Typez demo or the cursor navigation guide.

Apple’s Text Replacement is useful for shortcuts. Typez instead lets you deliberately import and pin text to reuse from a visible list inside the keyboard. Other third-party keyboards, including SwiftKey, also offer saved-text features.
numbers-and-layout
Typing features and customization

If your priority is predictions and autocorrection, choose a keyboard that supports them in your language. Typez currently does not support autocorrection; its focus is editing, a permanent number row, saved text and customization.

For number-heavy typing, see our number-row guide. If you often type in several languages, check each keyboard’s current language coverage before installing it.
permissions-and-integration
Are third-party iPhone keyboards safe to use?

Review each developer’s privacy policy, especially how it handles typed text and any network or analytics access. Full Access expands a keyboard extension’s permissions; the warning alone does not establish what a particular developer collects.

Typez’s core typing and cursor controls work without Full Access. Its optional clipboard requires it. The policy states that typing and clipboard contents are not uploaded or used in analytics; saved items stay local. Read the privacy policy and the Full Access explanation.

iOS can still display Apple’s keyboard in secure fields or apps that reject custom keyboards.
choose-your-workflow
Is a third-party keyboard worth it?

Keep Apple’s keyboard if it already meets your needs. Try an alternative if a specific daily task is frustrating: swipe typing, suggestions, entering numbers, editing text or inserting repeated phrases.

You can keep multiple keyboards enabled and choose the one that suits the task. Explore Typez and check its current availability if precise editing and saved text are your priorities.

articles.title: Best iPhone Keyboards in 2026: 4 Options Compared
articles.description: Compare Apple Keyboard, Gboard, Microsoft SwiftKey and Typez for cursor controls, clipboard, number rows, predictions, customization and pricing on iPhone.
articles.deck: Choose a keyboard based on what you actually want to improve.
articles.answer: Apple’s built-in keyboard is the default choice for system integration. Gboard is an option for glide typing and emoji search, while SwiftKey offers predictions, swipe typing and saved clips. Typez focuses on precise cursor controls, a number row and saved text, but currently lacks autocorrection.
sections: how-we-chose
Four iPhone keyboards worth comparing

This is a feature-based shortlist written by the creator of Typez, not an independent review or a measured speed test. It compares the iPhone versions specifically. We use official product listings and support pages; unconfirmed features are marked rather than assumed from Android.
feature-comparison

“Not verified” means the cited iOS sources did not establish the feature; it is not a claim that the feature is absent. Prices and availability can vary by country and change over time.
apple-keyboard
Apple Keyboard: best starting point for most iPhone users

Already installed, Apple’s keyboard supports system text editing, autocorrection, predictions and swipe typing in supported languages. Try the spacebar trackpad and Text Replacement before deciding you need an alternative.

Best fit: everyday typing with minimal setup. Trade-off: the standard English letter layout lacks a permanent number row and a dedicated cursor-arrow row.
gboard
Gboard: for glide typing and Google tools

Gboard for iPhone offers glide typing, emoji and GIF search, and other Google-oriented features. It is listed as free on the US App Store.

Best fit: users who prefer gesture typing and Gboard’s search tools. Trade-off: do not assume its iOS version has all the clipboard or layout features found on Android.
swiftkey
Microsoft SwiftKey: for predictions and swipe typing

Microsoft SwiftKey for iPhone emphasizes learned predictions, autocorrection, swipe input and themes. Microsoft also documents an iOS clipboard that can save clips and an optional permanent number row.

Best fit: users who value predictions and want a customizable keyboard with saved text. Trade-off: review its optional account features, language support and privacy settings.
typez
Typez: for precise editing and saved text

Typez gives you buttons to move the cursor one character or word at a time, a number row and a clipboard for deliberately imported and pinned text. It also offers themes, fonts and feedback preferences.

Best fit: users who frequently edit URLs, addresses, codes or small typos, or repeatedly paste saved phrases. Trade-off: autocorrection is not supported at present. Clipboard access requires Full Access, while core typing and cursor navigation do not.

Check Typez’s current availability and see the demo. For a broader comparison, read Apple keyboard vs third-party keyboards.
make-your-own-comparison
Which iPhone keyboard should you choose?

Try the same five tasks in each keyboard: write a normal sentence, type a specialist word, fix one character in the middle of a word, enter a mixed address, and insert a frequently used phrase. Compare the experience in your own language and favorite apps.

Pick the keyboard that helps with your actual workflow, not the one with the longest feature list. Before enabling Full Access, check the developer’s privacy policy and what features need it.
